newsitem.title: PERU: Colombia devaluation could reach 29 pct - cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Colombia devaluation could reach 29 pct - cenbank.

text.p: Colombia's central bank hopes to limit the peso's devaluation this year against the dollar to no more than 29 percent, keeping the currency within its exchange band, general manager Miguel Urrutia said Wednesday.

"The central bank is capable of defending the exchange band that has a devaluation set for this year of a minimum of 15 percent," Urrutia said in an interview. "(The devaluation) may reach up to a maximum of 29 percent."
The exchange rate band has a fixed maximum devaluation of 32.3 percent.
Urrutia said the bank estimated Colombia's inflation would be 18 percent this year, but hoped the rate would be lower.
"It would be magnificent if inflation were below 18 percent," he said.
The bank also expects to increase its net international reserves this year by about $750 million because of private investment and increased oil revenue, Urrutia said.
The country's net foreign reserves reached an all-time high of $9.935 billion as of March 21, up from $9.896 billion at the beginning of the year.
